The main takeaway from our work is that
the gastric phenotype may be present in the esophagogastric junction, and this should be taken into account in the differential diagnosis of esophageal adenocarcinomas.
the presence of gastric foveolae in Barrett's esophagitis should not be considered as a normal variant but as a premalignant lesion that requires close endoscopic follow-up.
in patients with Barrett's esophageal epithelium, the risk of developing esophageal adenocarcinomas of gastric phenotype should not be underestimated.
